collection.description: A stranger appears at the spring while a villager is filling jars, and asks, very politely, for water.

ask.text:
A stranger appears at the spring while (name) is filling jars, and asks, very politely, for water.
(Name) hands over a bowl. The stranger drinks it in one go. And another. And a third. When (name) asks, conversationally, where (he/she) has come from, the stranger goes quiet, and doesn't answer.
The stranger keeps glancing back toward the trees, over and over, as if expecting something to follow (him/her) out of them.
Nothing does. But (name) finds (himself/herself) glancing back at the trees too. (Name) wants to help, but should (he/she) ask what the stranger is running from?

choices.label: Offer Them a Place Among Us
Swap Water for a Day's Help

c1o1.text: The stranger drinks their fill and rests in the shade. After a while, some of the tension leaves (his/her) shoulders, and (he/she) stops looking at the trees quite so often. By evening, (he/she) is laughing at something a child said.

c1o2.text: The stranger shares a handful of wild berries gathered on the road, in a leaf, as thanks. It adds a little food. "They're safe," (he/she) adds quickly, seeing (name)'s face. They are.

c1.text: (Name) doesn't ask again. (He/She) just fills the stranger's water skin to the top, and points to a patch of shade...

c2o1.text: That, the stranger will talk about. (He/She) points out a faster trail to fresh water on the far side of the ridge, one nobody in the village knew about, through a gap in the rocks. It teaches the village something useful, and saves the water carriers a long walk in dry seasons.

c2o2.text: The stranger still won't say where (he/she) came from, and doesn't say much about the road either. No one insists. Some things, (name) decides, are not anyone else's business.

c2.text: Later, (name) asks again, more gently, not where the stranger came from, but how the road was...

c3o1.text: The stranger decides to stay, and joins the village permanently as a new adult villager. (He/She) settles in well, works hard, and is kind to the children. (He/She) still prefers not to talk about the trees, and never walks near them alone, and nobody ever asks why.

c3o2.text: The stranger thanks the village sincerely, and moves on before nightfall, walking quickly down the beach, away from the trees. (Name) watches until (he/she) is out of sight, and finds (himself/herself) hoping, very much, that the stranger gets wherever (he/she) is going.

c3.text: As dusk falls, (name) notices the stranger has nowhere to go. (He/She) offers a place by the fire, and more than that, if (he/she) wants it...

c4o1.text: The stranger helps carry the harvest in from the fields, basket after basket, without stopping, adding a good amount of food to the stores. (He/She) works as if staying busy is the only thing keeping (him/her) together.

c4o2.text: The villagers notice the stranger's water skin leaks badly, which explains the three bowls. They patch it with sap and send (him/her) onward with it full, and a bundle of food besides.

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c4.text: The stranger asks if there's any work (he/she) could do to pay for the water and a meal...
